signals.signal: The bank's own public location API returns 762 live ATMs on 30/07/2026 (685 distinct addresses), of which only 196 (25.7%) are flagged 'Has deposit functionality'; 512 are 24/7 and 673 contactless. 314 records are on-site 'UCB'-named units, so c.448 are off-site, concentrated at retail hosts (Kaufland 106+, Fantastiko 44+).
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bulbank - public locations API (/en/api/locations/atms.json, behind the Branches and ATMs locator)
signals.implies: Resolves the previously Low-confidence '~700+/755' fleet estimate with a machine-readable primary count, and quantifies the recycler white space: three quarters of the fleet is cash-out only in a country that adopted the euro on 01/01/2026. Direct opening for Printec cash-recycling/deposit-automation upgrades and for managed services on the large off-site retail estate.
signals.likelihood: High - deposit-capable share is the bank's own stated growth channel
signals.followup: Re-pull the API monthly to track deposit-capable count; ask the bank which units are recyclers vs deposit-only (cash-in), and who maintains the off-site retail estate.

signals.signal: Audited FY2025 separate financial statements: 'As of December 31, 2025 the Bank operates through its network comprising of 161 branches and remote locations.' The live locator returns 162 branch records on 30/07/2026, of which 31 carry the 'Cashless service' flag, 11 are Corporate, 8 Private Banking, 22 extended hours, 12 with safe vaults.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bulbank / UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts (Bulbank separate FS, Note 1) + UniCredit Bulbank locations API
signals.implies: Replaces the carried FY2024 '~125 branches' figure. The 31 cashless branches are the first hard count of the 'Branch of the Future' cashless model - each one displaces teller cash handling onto self-service, i.e. an addressable ATM/recycler and lobby-device requirement.
signals.followup: Track the cashless-flag count in the locator quarterly; establish which self-service hardware sits in each cashless branch.

signals.signal: The bank's FY2025 risk section lists its 2026 Non-Financial Risk watch-list as: extension of the anti-fraud system (SAS FM Tool) coverage; monitoring of Safer Payments system enhancements; a New Digital Onboarding solution; and - under ICT & ICT Security Risks - 'ATM obsolescence'. Euro-adoption post-go-live activities remain a 2026 focus.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - UniCredit Bulbank Activity Review, Risk Management, '2026 Outlook'
signals.implies: The bank itself names ATM obsolescence as a monitored 2026 ICT risk - the single strongest documented trigger for a fleet-replacement or managed-services conversation. It also names its incumbent fraud stack (SAS Fraud Management, ACI Safer Payments) and confirms a new digital onboarding solution is in flight, mapping to Printec eKYC/digital onboarding and transaction-monitoring/AML offers.
signals.likelihood: High for ATM refresh discussion in 6-12 months; onboarding solution may already be awarded
signals.followup: Find out whether the 'New Digital Onboarding solution' is a Group-mandated build or a local procurement, and whether ATM obsolescence has an approved remediation budget for 2026-27.

signals.signal: Accounting-estimate change in FY2025: 'The useful life of ATM machines (within item Fixtures and fittings) was changed in 2025 financial year from 5 to 7 years due to the improved maintenance practices, technological stability and historical performance data', applied prospectively under IAS 8.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - UniCredit Bulbank separate FS, accounting policies (property and equipment)
signals.implies: Plain English: the bank now writes ATMs off over 7 years instead of 5, i.e. it intends to keep machines in service longer and it credits 'improved maintenance practices' for that. This is a direct argument for a multi-year managed-services/maintenance contract rather than a capex swap-out - and it sits in tension with the 'ATM obsolescence' risk flag, which is the wedge to use.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - shapes how any refresh will be financed
signals.followup: Identify the current ATM maintenance provider whose 'improved maintenance practices' justified the life extension - this is the incumbent to displace or partner with.

signals.signal: Group-level channel programme: 'we are implementing a major ATM renewal plan, replacing more than half of our machines with latest-generation models by 2027'; almost 90% of UniCredit branches have been upgraded to date; BancoSmart 2.0 ATM interface launched in 2025 on cash-withdrawal-only ATMs, being distributed to Advanced (deposit) ATMs, with arrival on Quick Cash Desks expected in 2026.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - 'Acceleration in Action', Channels (October, Italy)
signals.implies: A dated, Group-committed replacement of >50% of the ATM estate by 2027 gives Bulbank's 762 machines a plausible refresh envelope of c.380+ units, plus a software/interface migration wave. Printec self-service, deployment and managed services all map; note the item is written from an Italy/Group perspective so the Bulgarian share is not disclosed.
signals.likelihood: Medium - Group plan is stated; Bulgarian allocation unconfirmed
signals.followup: Confirm whether Bulbank is inside the Group ATM renewal plan and whether procurement is Group-central (Italy) or local; check if BancoSmart 2.0 is live on Bulgarian ATMs.

signals.signal: Cash logistics jumped through the euro changeover: 'Cash in hand and in ATM' BGN 390,464 thousand at 31/12/2025 vs BGN 270,831 thousand at 31/12/2024 (+44%); 'Cash in transit' BGN 423,033 thousand vs BGN 211,564 thousand (+100%). The bank also states it holds the No.1 market share in amounts deposited via the ATM network, with deposited amounts up c.20% year on year.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - Bulbank separate FS Note 22 'Cash and balances with Central Bank'; Retail activity review
signals.implies: Cash held in machines and in transit doubled during the changeover while only 196 ATMs can take deposits. That combination - rising cash volumes on a mostly cash-out fleet - is the classic business case for recyclers (a recycler re-uses deposited notes for withdrawals, cutting CIT trips) and for cash-cycle optimisation software/managed services.
signals.likelihood: High - cash volumes are disclosed and rising
signals.followup: Quantify CIT cost per machine and pitch a recycler business case on the 566 cash-out-only units.

signals.signal: PRIME, a new personal-banking service model, was launched on 18/05/2026 simultaneously in nine CEE countries (Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia) under the Group 'UniCredit Unlimited' strategic plan. In Bulgaria it targets clients with assets above EUR 50,000, regular income above EUR 3,100/month in Sofia and above EUR 2,600 elsewhere; it includes a dedicated PRIME section in Bulbank Mobile with a personal PRIME banker and priority service in branches and the contact centre.
signals.implies: Confirms and sharpens the baseline 'Prime zones' item: PRIME is a service model with in-branch priority zones, not just a segment badge. Branch re-fits to create PRIME areas free up floorspace that is typically backfilled with self-service/recycler zones - and priority servicing raises the bar on branch queue/lobby technology.
signals.followup: Establish how many branches will be physically re-fitted for PRIME in 2026-27 and whether lobby self-service is part of the fit-out spec.

signals.signal: On 24/06/2026 the bank extended free exchange of Bulgarian lev banknotes and coins in its branch network to 30/09/2026, and announced it will offer SEPA Instant Payments from 20/08/2026. A declaration on the origin of funds is required for exchanges above EUR 5,000.
signals.implies: Six months after euro adoption the bank is still absorbing legacy-lev cash over the counter - branch cash-handling load has not normalised, which sustains the case for teller cash recyclers (TCRs) and back-office note/coin processing. The 20/08/2026 SEPA Instant go-live raises real-time payment volumes and therefore real-time fraud/transaction-monitoring load.
signals.followup: Check after 30/09/2026 whether the free-exchange window is extended again; test appetite for TCRs in the cash-serving branches.

signals.signal: The Google Cloud partnership entered in 2025 covers all 13 banks in the Group, migrating large parts of the application landscape including legacy systems, and establishes Google Cloud as UniCredit's primary platform for AI workloads using Vertex AI and Gemini; named application areas include financial crime prevention, operational process optimisation and customer interactions, plus possible use of Google Maps platform.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - 'Digital and Data' / Google Cloud partnership (May, Group)
signals.implies: Re-verifies the baseline '10-year Google Cloud incl. financial crime on Vertex AI' against the primary annual report (the report confirms scope = all 13 banks and financial-crime AI, but does not state a 10-year term). Any Printec AML/transaction-monitoring or HSM/security proposition into Bulbank must be cloud-native and interoperable with a Google Cloud/Vertex AI target architecture.
signals.likelihood: High - contract signed, migration under way
signals.followup: Confirm the contract term (10 years is not stated in the annual report) and whether local financial-crime tooling is being consolidated onto the Group Vertex AI platform.

signals.signal: FY2025 headcount fell from 3,134 to 3,038 FTEs at bank level (3,582 to 3,455 consolidated), explicitly 'in alignment with the Strategic plan, driven by continuous investments in digitalization'. In parallel the Real Estate team's 2025 priorities were 'the development of self-service zones, agency branches, optimization of spaces', 16,000 archive boxes were relocated out of the branch network, and the bank says it will 'continue Agent model roll-out' in 2026 to keep access in smaller towns.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - UniCredit Bulbank Activity Review (People, Real Estate, Retail outlook)
signals.implies: Staff down 3.1% while the physical footprint is held: the gap is being closed by self-service zones and an agent model (third-party outlets acting for the bank in small towns). Both are device-led - unmanned self-service zones need 24/7-hardened ATMs/recyclers and remote monitoring, exactly Printec's managed-services proposition.
signals.followup: Get the number of agency branches and self-service zones opened in 2025 and planned for 2026 - not disclosed in the report.

signals.signal: FY2025 card and acceptance metrics: POS fleet +6%, merchants using the acquiring service +13.6%, POS acquiring volumes +13.5%; debit card transactions +15%, credit card +19%, ATM transactions +4%, POS transactions +12%; newly issued fully digital debit cards +33% y/y; digital sales through Bulbank Mobile +26% y/y.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - UniCredit Bulbank Activity Review (Retail, cards and POS)
signals.implies: Acceptance is growing three times faster than ATM usage (+12% POS transactions vs +4% ATM). The POS estate is expanding (+6%) with merchant numbers up 13.6% - a live POS/acquiring terminal-estate and terminal-management-services opportunity, and a reason to pitch ATM value-add (deposit, FX, bill-pay replacement) rather than pure cash-out capacity.
signals.followup: Obtain the absolute POS terminal count (percentage only is disclosed) and identify the terminal estate manager / TMS incumbent.

signals.entity: Bulgarian banking sector (context for UniCredit Bulbank)
signals.signal: 'To facilitate a smooth transition to the euro, local commercial banks invested more than BGN 400 mln in system adaptation, staff training, and the organization of information campaigns' - and 'Commercial banks upgraded their IT infrastructure, payment systems, and ATMs, ensuring that all operations could be conducted in euros from the first day.'
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - 'Bulgarian banking sector in 2025'
signals.implies: Sizes the euro-changeover IT spend pool across the Bulgarian market at >BGN 400m (>EUR 204m at the fixed 1.95583 rate) and confirms ATMs were adapted (software/cassette conversion) rather than wholesale replaced in 2025 - so the hardware replacement wave is still ahead, not behind.
signals.likelihood: Medium - post-changeover hardware refresh is a 2026-28 question
signals.followup: Cross-check the BGN 400m figure against BNB or Association of Banks in Bulgaria publications.

signals.signal: On 09/07/2026 UniCredit and Alpha Bank announced they are deepening their strategic partnership on regional markets with a specific focus on Bulgaria, following a meeting of both management teams at UniCredit Bulbank's Sofia head office; quoted are Teodora Petkova (UniCredit Head of Central and Eastern Europe) and Lazaros Papagaryfallou (Alpha Bank Deputy CEO).
signals.implies: A cross-border Greece-Bulgaria corporate platform, not an M&A event - but it links the Greek Alpha relationship (where Printec is an ATM partner) to the Bulgarian entity, a useful reference route into Bulbank.
signals.likelihood: Medium - commercial cooperation, no infrastructure implication yet
signals.followup: Use the Alpha Greece relationship as an introduction path into UniCredit Bulbank procurement.

signals.signal: Channel automation delivered in 2025: a new voice-bot virtual assistant 'Niki' piloted in the Contact Center at end-2025; a new automatic customer identification process using IVR plus the mobile app to identify callers before an operator answers; a biometric-powered self-reactivation flow in Bulbank Mobile; a Virtual Mortgage Center launched in Q4-2025 with end-to-end video consultation, digital signing and disbursement; and 'Comfort by UniCredit', a rebranded fully remote servicing model with a personal remote banker.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2025 Annual Reports and Accounts - UniCredit Bulbank Activity Review (Contact Center, Virtual Region)
signals.implies: Remote identification via biometrics and video, plus a stated 'New Digital Onboarding solution' for 2026, is precisely the digital onboarding/eKYC and identity-verification stack Printec sells; the identity layer is being built now, which is the moment to engage.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - onboarding refresh is an explicit 2026 item
signals.followup: Determine the vendor behind the biometric self-reactivation and the planned digital onboarding solution.

signals.entity: Bulgarian ATM/POS market (context for UniCredit Bulbank)
signals.signal: BNB payment statistics: 5,031 ATM terminal devices in Bulgaria at 31/12/2025, down from 5,087 at end-2024, 5,064 at end-H1-2025 and a 2016 peak of 5,751. POS terminals rose to 210,861 at 31/12/2025 from 163,190 at end-2024 (+29.2%). In H2-2025 there were 60.7 million card cash-withdrawal operations worth EUR 13.7bn against only 5.8 million card cash-deposit operations worth EUR 3.7bn.
signals.source_name: Bulgarian National Bank - Payment statistics for Bulgaria, main indicators (ps_mainindicators_new_eur_bg.xlsx, annual and half-year sheets)
signals.implies: UniCredit Bulbank's 762 ATMs are c.15.1% of the national fleet. The market is shrinking in ATM units but exploding in acceptance points (+47,671 POS in one year), and cash-deposit operations are only 9.6% of withdrawal operations nationally - the clearest market-wide evidence that deposit automation/recycling is under-built in Bulgaria, which is exactly the gap Printec recyclers address, alongside a very large POS estate opportunity.
signals.followup: Re-pull the same XLSX after the H1-2026 update to see the first full post-euro half-year of ATM counts and deposit volumes.

signals.entity: BORICA AD / OpenWay (national card and ATM infrastructure)
signals.signal: On 23/07/2026 BORICA AD and OpenWay announced two Global Transaction Banking Innovation Awards 2026 (The Digital Banker) for Bulgaria's euro payments transition. The release states OpenWay's Way4 platform provides the national card infrastructure for authorisation and payment processing, card issuing, merchant servicing, card switching, ATM and POS device management, fraud prevention and transaction processing, across a programme involving more than 35 banks and PSPs. In the first 48 hours after euro adoption the infrastructure processed over 930,000 card and ATM transactions worth close to EUR 42 million with no unplanned outage; the first euro ATM withdrawal occurred 20 seconds after midnight.
signals.implies: Maps the incumbent layer any Bulgarian ATM proposition must sit under: ATM and POS device management and fraud screening for the national scheme run on OpenWay Way4 at BORICA. Printec ATM/managed-services and monitoring offers into UniCredit Bulbank must integrate with, not replace, that switch - and the fraud-prevention module is a competitive overlap to be aware of.
signals.followup: Confirm whether UniCredit Bulbank drives its ATMs through BORICA's Way4 switch or through a UniCredit Group processor.

signals.signal: The bank's own locator flags 532 of its 762 ATMs as 'Accessible (ground floor/ramp)' but 212 as 'Access with assistance required'. Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act) expressly covers automated teller machines among self-service terminals; its requirements apply to products placed on the market after 28/06/2025, while self-service terminals already in use may continue to be used until the end of their economic life and in any case for no longer than 20 years.
signals.source_name: UniCredit Bulbank locations API + Directive (EU) 2019/882 (European Accessibility Act), EUR-Lex
signals.implies: 28% of the fleet is self-declared as needing assistance to access. Every machine the bank now replaces must meet the Accessibility Act specification, so the accessibility rules convert the 'ATM obsolescence' risk into a compliance-timed replacement argument rather than a discretionary one - a strong framing for a Printec fleet-refresh proposal.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no Bulgarian enforcement action seen; obligation bites on replacement
signals.followup: Check the Bulgarian transposition act and whether any national supervisory body has published an ATM accessibility timetable; the exact article numbers of the transitional provision were not verified.

signals.signal: UniCredit's 2Q26 group results were approved on 22/07/2026 and released in Milan on 23/07/2026: net profit EUR 2.9bn in 2Q26 and EUR 6.3bn in 1H26. The press release contains no branch, ATM or Bulgaria-segment profit disclosure - Bulgaria appears only in sovereign-exposure and duration tables. A secondary report puts UniCredit's net profit from operations in Bulgaria at EUR 251 million in 1H-2026, down 1.5% year on year.
signals.source_name: UniCredit 2Q26 Group Results press release (primary, PDF) + SeeNews (secondary, for the Bulgaria figure)
signals.implies: Bulgarian earnings are flat-to-slightly-down against a record group, which tightens the local cost lens - favourable to opex-based managed services and unfavourable to large local capex. Note the EUR 251m Bulgaria figure is aggregator-sourced and was not found in the primary press release.
signals.followup: Pull the 2Q26 Group databook/divisional annex to source the Bulgaria segment figure primarily; the press release alone does not carry it.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed). Primary sources actually opened: UniCredit Bulbank financial-reports index and the FY2025 annual report PDF (curl with desktop Chrome UA, pdfminer text extraction) - this is the report that carries both the Group narrative and the Bulbank Activity Review and separate financial statements; the bank's four public locations JSON endpoints (atms, branches, nomenclatures, services), which are the entry point that finally resolved the branch and ATM counts and gave the deposit-capable and cashless-branch splits; three pages of the Bulgarian-language newsroom with per-article <time> dates (covering roughly March to July 2026); the corporate ATM product page; BNB payment statistics XLSX (annual, half-year and quarterly sheets); BORICA newsroom; UniCredit Group 2Q26 press-release PDF; EUR-Lex for Directive (EU) 2019/882. Deliberate variation from previous runs: this run went at the bank through its own undocumented locator JSON APIs and through the BNB statistical XLSX rather than through press coverage, which is what produced the hard counts. Genuine gaps: (1) the ATM OEM / maintenance incumbent at UniCredit Bulbank remains UNIDENTIFIED after four angles (English and Bulgarian vendor press, procurement-style wording, bank site, OEM newsrooms) - carrying it forward as the standing task; (2) absolute POS terminal count for the bank is not disclosed, only percentage growth; (3) the number of agency branches and self-service zones opened in 2025 and planned for 2026 is described but not quantified anywhere in the annual report; (4) no H1-2026 Bulbank-level financial statement is published on the bank's IR pages - the site carries annual reports and Pillar III disclosures only, so no post-FY2025 branch or ATM count exists from the bank itself; (5) the Google Cloud contract term (baseline said 10 years) is NOT stated in the annual report and could not be primary-verified this run.
access_issues: unicreditbulbank.bg returns 403 to default fetch agents; resolved by curl with a desktop Chrome User-Agent (per the source-catalogue hint) - no source was dropped. The 20 MB FY2025 annual-report PDF timed out in an inline pdfminer call and had to be extracted in a background job. unicreditgroup.eu returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch on the 2Q26 press-release HTML page; the same content was obtained as a PDF via curl with a browser UA. borica.bg article URLs guessed from press coverage 404 - the newsroom index had to be scraped for the real slug, and the December-2025 BORICA monthly statistics release could not be located on borica.bg (the '+85% ATM deposits to EUR 471m in December' figure exists only in secondary Bulgarian press and is therefore NOT reported as a signal). The scratchpad is shared with sibling agents, so an unrelated Banca Transilvania PDF briefly collided with the filename 'ar2025.pdf'; all files were re-namespaced with a ucb_ prefix and the collision did not contaminate any finding.
operator_requests: none - every source used was retrievable. If an operator has a moment: the BORICA monthly payment-statistics releases (the December-2025 one showing ATM deposits +85% to EUR 471m) are cited widely in Bulgarian press but were not findable on borica.bg; a direct link would let that figure be promoted from press to primary.
